items.title: Yourself.Bet
items.summary: Gather 'round. Grab a notepad. Pencil. Dropping nuggets. He on the…
items.content_html:
Gather 'round.

Grab a notepad.

Pencil.

Dropping nuggets.

He on the can again?

Let me ask you a question.

What's the most asymmetric bet?

What's the best investment?

Stocks?

Index funds?

CDs?

Angel investing?

Venture?

Crypto?

Yeah, yeah.

All that's fine and dandy.

But it ain't even close.

To the best.

So what's the most asymmetric bet?

The bet on you.

The most asymmetric bet is the bet you make on yourself.

Now I'm not saying go Pete Rose, here.

Love ya, Charlie!

But I'm kinda saying go Pete Rose, here.

You think that man lacked confidence in himself?

A lot of you probably have no idea who Pete Rose is, so just insert another name more contemporary that fits a mother mother who has a lot of confidence in themselves.

The day the lights turned on upstairs for yours truly was when I realized it doesn't matter what anyone else thinks, it matters what I think.

And what I think can move mountains.

Has moved mountains.

Moves mountains to this day.

Chopped 'em down with the edge of my hand.

I'm not a gambling man.

But I do make bets.

Every day.

Asymmetrical ones.

Orthogonal ones.

And baby, there ain't no bet more asymmetrical, more orthogonal, than all in on me.

Make a bet today.

Yourself.Bet.

What are they going to do?

Ban you for life?

Okay, maybe they will.

But what's the alternative?

You gonna bet on Elon?

Probably not a bad idea.

You gonna bet on artificially super intel?

Big fan.

Bet on God?

Sounds like the right answer if it's not blasphemous to do so.

If God bet on you, would that change things?

Always has. Always does. Always will.

You don't bet on the odds, you bet on yourself.

The odds are against you, and believe me, you wouldn't want it any other way.

Underdogs always pay the biggest.

🏦

Mustard seed faith.

That's all I'm asking.

.

🚽

🧻

[Flush.]

items.title: Niche Please
items.summary: Wanna get big? Not super big. Little big. I think that's…
items.content_html:
Wanna get big?

Not super big.

Little big.

I think that's what you're striving for.

A little big.

Listen, you know who you're talking to?

The grandjack of all trades.

And I want to tell you that being the grandmaster of one little slice of this magnificent Actuverse is how you "make" it.

Some folks call it finding your niche.

Scratching your itch.

Don't be a ...

You get the idea.

I don't even think you need 1,000 true fans anymore.

More like fiddy.

Heck, even the right one can change your life.

My niche right now is old(ish) curmudgeon musings column.

With a side of joy.

Because part of the gimmick is that it's all an act.

Which one is the real me?

Ahh, so.

🦗

Where the riches?

I heard they here.

I don't see sheet.

items.title: Interpopping And Locking
items.summary: If I could offer you one piece of advice, it wouldn't…
items.content_html:
If I could offer you one piece of advice, it wouldn't be to wear sunscreen.

So what would it be?

I don't know.

I'm thinking about it.

[Staring at horizon.]

I've always considered myself a wise man.

Wise arse more like it.

All true.

But as I've fermented like a fine, stanky, kimchi, I've matured a little.

A little stanky.

A little mature.

But I don't know if I could offer one piece of advice.

Because I'm generally in the hundreds.

Hundreds of pieces.

And that these pieces piece together to solve a puzzle.

The puzzle of you.

You might find that as you're putting it together, it's beautiful.

Or you might be horrified to see what it is making.

So if I could offer you one piece, it'd be this:

You are a puzzling mother mother.

We all are.

Built piece by piece.

🧩

But I don't think there's ever been two identical puzzles.

So you got that going for you.

Which is nice.

My advice then is:

Build a puzzle that is a grandmasterpiece.

An Apex Opus.

Your highest work.

I'd say make a Mona Lisa but I don't think she's all that special.

There I said it.

You can do better than that.

You can always remove or add pieces.

Even shake the box and start all over.

If you're doing that, I'd suggest one thing:

Find your corner pieces.

And build out from there.

📐

items.title: Confidence Par Excellence
items.summary: "How confident are you in carrying this team forward?" "One thing…
items.content_html:
"How confident are you in carrying this team forward?"

"One thing that I do...is forgetting those...that is behind...and reaching forward...to what's ahead."

[Stares at horizon.]

[Stares at horizon.]

[Single tear.]

Poetry.

💧

"We are our brother's keeper. Winning this game for Jaxson. You know, um, 12 points. 6 x 2. It's for you. That's 12."

Jaxson Dart is the starting QB who got hurt last week and is out for the season. The Giants scored 12 points and won. Dart's uniform number is 6.

I don't know what's going to happen the rest of the season, but I am in!

Might I suggest higher multiples of 6, though?

items.title: Painting Metrics
items.summary: You would think, as studious as I am, that I'd be…
items.content_html:
You would think, as studious as I am, that I'd be a data guy.

Crunching unctuous numbers.

But you'd be wrong.

Because I'm an art guy.

Vibes, baby.

Not a science.

You see, it's because data often lies.

Take for example, football stats.

Guy throws an interception. 

Looks bad right?

On paper.

But what if it only happened because it went right through the wide receiver's hands?

Thrown perfectly, not caught.

INT.

Numbers sometimes tell a story, but not the whole story.

And so a QB could have a great night but it doesn't look like it through no fault of his own.

The trick then is, as a QB of life, to not lose confidence if you know you're doing everything right.

Just like you shouldn't get too big for your britches because your teammates make spectacular catches on your bad throws.

It's a numbers game.

But the science is in the art. 

Numbers tell the truth.

But not the whole truth.

I swear.

So help me, God.

Keep slingin'.

items.title: It's Not A Triangle, It's A Pyramid!
items.summary: There's this idea that you shouldn't trust anyone that doesn't skin…
items.content_html:
There's this idea that you shouldn't trust anyone that doesn't skin in the game.

I generally stop the thought at "anyone."

The idea being if someone is hawking the virtues of X, said hawker should have a vested interest in X.

So if X is a success, we all cheer. If it fails, hawker and you sad.

But there's something off here, right?

This idea is flawed.

Particularly if you understand that they are only hawking because they own it.

They have a biased opinion.

An interested interest.

Rhymes with Fonzie.

If they didn't have skin in the game, they wouldn't give two sheets.

About you or it.

💩💩

And so the balance is weighing the value of skin.

Are they hawking because they believe?

Or because they have to?

Because they have skin and they really gotta make sure this hits?

There are a lot of carnival barkers out there.

Just barking.

And it's got me thinking.

Oh no.

Why the hard sell?

If it's so good, why share?

Why is it so pivotal that we jump on the wagon?

Is it truly because you're enlightened?

Or is it because if we join, you get richer?

When I was in college, there was a buddy of a buddy who had this motivational cassette he wanted me to listen to.

It'll change your life!

So I listened.

It was a dude speaking to a live audience about how he made it.

And about how you could make it too.

How?

By selling.

Convincing your friends and family to buy sheet from you.

But do you want to get really rich?

Convince them to convince their friends and family to buy from them!

You don't even have to lift a finger!!!

I'm listening.

It was a fine tape.

And perhaps I mocked my friend of a friend too much after listening.

But he never brought that sheet to me again.

The line I remember from the tape was something along the lines of, "If your friends sold toothpaste, why wouldn't you buy toothpaste from them?"

And I thought, this dude who gave me the tape is many things, but I wouldn't trust them(.) on toothpaste vouching.

And so the takeaway is this.

Having skin in the game is often a plus.

Having skin in the game is often a minus.

Wisdom, wissmart, is knowing the difference.

Judgment will always be a human skill.

Godly.

Filtering.

Having all the facts before you, and making the call.

Are they selling because they would love for you to see the light?

Angels.

Or are they selling because they need you to help keep them on?

Something else.

🔦

items.title: Winners and Losers
items.summary: One of my favorite authors, back in the day, was a…
items.content_html:
One of my favorite authors, back in the day, was a fellow who would write about his life.

He was a kind of down on his luck fellow.

Who marched to his own beat and never fit in anywhere.

But he would find a place with fellow beat marchers wherever he went.

And he went a lot of places.

He was in search of answers.

Like a lot of us.

And so he wrote about them.

Like a lot of us should.

He wrote about how his first book didn't sell.

And that that was how he became a successful author.

For you see, the books that didn't sell were sold for pennies on the dollar to a discounter liquidator that ultimately were bought by someone who used them to fill the back book sections of truck stops.

Next to trashy romance novels.

And you know what happened?

Oldish ladies started buying his books back there.

They, some not all, picked it over Fabio.

And, as they say on the race track, they're off!

He became a pretty successful author with a very niche following.

Wrote a whole bunch of good books.

But then, almost in a blink, he turned into this business guru.

Telling everyone what to do.

And he became huge(ish).

Writing all about how to run a business.

How to tell a story.

He became a brand.

Never writing books like he used to.

About his journey.

About his life.

And I always thought "Wow, good for him. But why not write the old way, too?"

And I learned that the reason he stopped was simple:

"I didn't want to be Loser ____ [his first name] anymore."

He said that many people would tell him how much they missed the old book style.

But that he was over it.

That he wasn't that guy anymore.

He didn't want to be that guy anymore.

He was a success!

And what makes me sad about it all, really, is that he thought that dude was a loser.

Because really, really, I think he has it all backwards.

When I last looked him up, he was kicking butt.

Owning stages.

Owning pods.

Owning and selling books.

Courses.

Upsells to corporate entities where eager people have large budgets and no skin in the game so they are itching to spend it.

Easy pickings.

I walked as far as I could as he transformed.

As he changed.

And when he became a little too, hmm what's the word, certain?

I had to part ways.

I missed the old ways.

I missed Winner ____.

And it made me a lil sad to think he saw it a different way.

To winners and losers.

And how we define them.

And to telling good stories.

And learning how to write them.

And to truck stops who still have spinny things in the back that hold books.

Have you ever considered carrying Highest Success?

I could get you a really good deal.

Winner!!!

items.title: Guests In My Corn
items.summary: "You mean out?" "Yeah. Out." "Far out." Since you all come…
items.content_html:
"You mean out?"

"Yeah. Out."

"Far out."

Since you all come here for advice.

[Covers mic.]

Why do people come here?

They probably typed "iterating.com" into their browser to see where it went.

Oh right.

[Uncovers mic.]

Since you all come to iterating.com because you love me, because you long to hear what I have to say, here's another gem.

Polished and gleaming.

Find a subject you love that everyone around you seems to think is a terrible, just terrible, waste of time.

Why?

Well, for one, it ticks off folks.

Which is terrible, but kinda hilarious.

But I also think it's indicative of you.

The pure you.

To love something that no one around you seems to.

Of course, it could be your way of rebelling.

Or being an arse.

I just love stomping on the floor above you, it gives me a tremendous sense of self-satisfaction.

Too early to tell.

But love what you love.

Within reason of course.

So the next time you catch yourself in another deep rabbit hole, taking a pill from Larry Fishy (don't take pills from Larry Fishy, bad idea. Or anything from people wearing long leather coats and pince-nez sunglasses. Trust.).

💊

Trust.

Where was I?

That was a terrible sentence up there.

And that's what I'm saying.

A lot of people, I daresay most, would come here and hate vehemently dislike the way I write.

From the old(ish) man ramblings, the single sentence paragraphs, and the incessant inability to call myself old(ish) without adding the -ish in parentheses at the end.

It's just not for everyone.

I didn't make it for everyone.

Why did you make it?

I made it to help me.

If it helps one other person:

Incredible.

Two?

Fantastic.

Three??

Dare to dream.

Four???

Getting greedy.

Look, what I'm saying is keep reading this sheet, no matter how many people ask you:

"Why in the world are you reading this sheet?"

But seriously.

Seriously.

I have to be here.

Why are you here?

Is it 'cause I built it?

"Wait a second. Wait a second. Why him? I built this field. You wouldn't be here if it wasn't for me. Well you wouldn't..."

"Ray for God's sake. I'm unattached. You have a family."

"I know! But I wanna know what's out there. I wanna see it."

"But you're not invited."

"Not invited? What do you mean I'm not invited? That's my corn out there. You guys are guests in my corn."

"Ray..."

"No, wait! I have done everything I have been asked to do. I didn't understand it but I've done it. And I haven't once asked what's in it for me."

"What are you saying, Ray?"

"I'm saying, what's in it for me?"

"Is that why you did this? For you?" 

Yes. 

Hey! 

Joe!

Look what I found:

👟👟

items.title: A Perfect Circle
items.summary: Here's what I want you to do. Right now. Take some Japanese…
items.content_html:
Here's what I want you to do.

Right now.

Take some Japanese Korean chalk and draw a circle on the ground.

No, this ain't some weird thing.

But it kinda is.

It kinda is.

Work with me.

Draw a big circle.

Done?

Ok, now say to yourself, "This is my circle."

Inside it, put everything you value.

Now, say, "Everything in this circle, I will defend with my life."

Hopefully, you remove some things from the circle.

Maybe add a thing or two.

I dunno, it's your circle.

Two things I hope you notice:

1. Not a lot of stuff in that circle.

2. You're in the circle.

So what's in the circle?

More importantly, who's in there?

I see a few things you're missing.

And I think a few things that should get the boot.

You know what and who I'm talking about.

You know.

C'mon.

Defend with your life!?

Really?

Really??

That thing/person [trying to sound specific but really being vague to appeal to mass(ish) audience]?

Alright, alright.

Your circle.

©️

Do with it as you please.

No.

Don't do that.

Do this:

Build a keep around this circle.

This is your soul.

And by golly, we are protecting this mother with all our might.

As you grow, you add moats and make them wider and wider around the keep.

Build cannons and towers and sheet.

Over time, things can earn entrance into the circle.

And, sadly, things should leave.

I cannot tell you how sacred this circle is.

It's about as holy as you'll make it.

But really?

That?

That makes the inner orbis??

Ah well.

At least you made it.

So long, and thanks for all the fish.

🐬

items.title: Good For Something
items.summary: I gotta tell you. This old(ish) curmudgeon gimmick is hard. Putting…
items.content_html:
I gotta tell you.

This old(ish) curmudgeon gimmick is hard.

Putting on the grimaced furrow and constant outrage.

Because the truth is, I am pretty (and) happy.

And it's hard to be pretty (and) happy and still swing your fists at the sun.

I mean I do it, but it's hard.

Middle-aged and crazy.

I got the whole world figured out, you know.

And my conclusion is:

I choose not to run!

Now, if you're one of those "change the world" types, you might view this as a weakness.

And that's fine.

That's fine.

Believe what you want.

Believe to achieve!

I gave up caring when I starting writing musings columns on the internet.

And I started that a long, long time ago.

In this galaxy.

But it still feels far away.

Although to be fair, I stopped for years at times because I did care.

For moments.

For seasons.

But alas, near death survival gives you something of a IDGAF attitude.

I call it gratitude.

I already sorta had that.

So it just stacked.

One on top of the other.

Stacking IDGAFs.

Highly recommend.

Within reason.

I always thought I was somewhat of a chaotic good lawyer, which, by definition, is probably not ideal.

Shoutout to my DND nerds.

It just sounds funny.

Chaotic good lawyer.

Makes me chuckle.

But if I'm honest, I'm probably neutral good.

A terrible name for a badarse alignment.

But it's what they call it.

I'm no longer practicing law, so I'm a neutral good something.

Just not sure what.

You know, we all shoot for great.

Strive for it, even.

But good's better.

Always has been, always will be.

Good's best.

My goodness.

Because you see, they're not on the same scale.

At least, not the way I see it.

Good isn't below great because they're not measuring the same thing.

I'm talking alignment good.

Not Jim Collins good.

Great to Good.

You might not see it yet, but if you do, if you do.

The world is yours.

Here.

🌏

Take it.

Just leave me a little slice.

🍕

For me and my tribe.

Somewhere by the water.

So I can cool the fire.

Be good, greatness.

"Have fun storming the castle!"

"Think it'll work?"

"It would take a miracle."

🏯

PS: "Slice" to me means the rest of the universe, multiverse, actuverse, whatever we're calling it. Too late, ink's dry. We used Uniball 207s to sign so I'm afraid it's binding forever.

Enjoy your blue marble.

CHAOTIC GOOD.
